title: Instrument-making and the best guitarists, Lorenzo Staulz and Willie Santiago
summary: St. Cyr made guitar parts for friends; he rates Lorenzo Staulz and himself uptown, and Joe Brooks and Willie Santiago downtown.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: I made a bandier guitar for Lorenzo Stahls. Out of a bandier.
You fixed one up for him too? Yeah, I made a make for him. You mentioned he was sort of your- I made one for a-
Well, for a Louis Capiton, I know him quite well too. Yeah.
I made a set of little, uh, Badger-Malentong, Bret Masley picture there. Yeah. I made the neck for that. Well, you did have that.
Yeah, you were writing this to him next. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah, you must have known them all, I guess. I never said it. Yes.

And he was the good ones, then the bad ones. Yeah. Yeah. Now, up- Uptown, Lorenzo Starrs and I, with the best guitar players. And, uh, downtown, Joe Brooks, you know, old days. Joe Brooks and Willie San Diego.
Willie San Diego was better than any of them.
He was better than any of them. I never got to know him. I almost met him in 1942. Somehow I didn't. And he was a very good mandolin player, too.
Willie San Diego was. He was a good bandoliner. He used to have a jam session. It's the only time he got to play the mandolin, you see? Oh, yeah.
And he liked the way I played the accompaniment on the guitar. And he used to have a jam session at his house with the mandolin. That's when you live downtown, too.
Oh yeah, it was in downtown. I lived on Columbus between Dave and Rome.
